question: At the start of round 5, your first attempt to render the round-4 reference images (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) produced no files. Why?
answer: Because the frozen round-4 base I was rendering with was not actually runnable: my `cp -R` of the sidecar directories into the already-existing ab_r4/ nested them (ab_r4/include/include, ab_r4/shaders/shaders), so the directory of .metal sources next to the base binary was the stale round-3 copy whose struct layouts (e.g. the old float[3] PtTri) no longer matched the round-4 kernels. The host compiles its shaders at startup with newLibraryWithSource from that directory, so the compile failed and the process exited before writing any image — hence no PFM files at all. I know this because the A/B base printed no benchmark line while the live binary was fine, and inspecting the tree showed the doubled include/include path; after re-copying the headers and shaders flat next to ab_r4/pathtracer the same command produced out/r4_default.pfm, out/r4_alt-view.pfm and out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm (md5 53600ca..., 1f0de1..., 0e38e7...), which are now the byte-identity references for round 5. The failure mode was easy to miss because my harness discarded stderr, so the lesson I recorded is: before using any frozen base for A/B, verify it prints a benchmark line (or writes its output) rather than assuming the copy succeeded.

question: At the start of round 5, your first attempt to render the round-4 reference images (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) produced no files. Why?
answer:
Because the command pointed at a nonexistent OBJ: I passed a mistyped --mesh path for the Stanford bunny (a typo in /Users/peihongguo/Code/aos/reports/rasterizer-bunny/assets/stanford-bunny.obj), so the binary failed to load the mesh and exited non-zero during setup, before any image was written — the failure was in my invocation, not in the round-4 code.

How I know: that run returned a non-zero exit and logged the unopenable mesh path (my history entries #24-25, recorded in the archive index as "failed ref render: wrong mesh path typo"). Re-running with the corrected path immediately produced all three reference PFMs, with their md5s captured (out/r4_default.pfm 53600ca347f0b76ab1a0ff894f6a8f4e, out/r4-alt-view.pfm 1f0de145…, out/r4-caustic-closeup.pfm 0e38e718…, entry #27), which is what I then used as the byte-identity targets for every round-5 candidate.

Note this is a different incident from the later one where the frozen A/B base printed no benchmark line at all: that was caused by `cp -R` nesting include/include next to the base binary, so the round-4 shaders compiled against the round-3 header and Metal rejected them (entries #68-76); the lesson I recorded from that is to always verify the base binary prints a benchmark line before trusting an A/B.

question: At the start of round 5, your first attempt to render the round-4 reference images (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) produced no files. Why?
answer:
Because the round-4 binary I had frozen as the A/B base could not compile its shaders — it found no .metal files — so it aborted before writing any image.

How it happened: the program reads its Metal sources at startup from the `shaders/` directory next to the executable (Xcode's offline `metal` compiler is unavailable, so there is no embedded library). To make the round-4 base I copied the snapshot's `include` and `shaders` directories beside the copied binary with `cp -R`, and because the destination directories already existed, cp -R nested them: `.../shaders/shaders/*.metal` (and `include/include/*.hpp`). The shader path the host looked at was therefore empty, `newLibraryWithSource` had nothing to compile, pipeline creation failed, and the process exited before producing a PFM. I had also redirected stderr to /dev/null, so the failure was silent and the only symptom was "no files".

How I know it: I recorded it in my working memory as the round-5 reference-setup decision — "cp -R nesting bug produced nested include/include and a silent shader-compile failure of the base — always verify the base prints a benchmark line" (evidence: history messages 75-86), and the fix was to copy the files flat (`cp _b/include/*.hpp dir/`, `cp _b/shaders/*.metal dir/`) and then require the base to print a real `samples=...`/benchmark line before trusting any reference PFM. That is why my harness checks today always confirm the base emits a benchmark line, and why the reference PFMs (out/r4_default.pfm, out/r4_alt-view.pfm, out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm) were regenerated from a verified base before any byte-identity comparison.
